code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# 1. Load data and filter
df = pd.read_parquet('train.parquet')
# keep only non-null QED_delta and SA_delta
df = df.dropna(subset=['QED_delta', 'SA_delta'])

# split into task 103 and others
df103 = df[df['task_id'] == 103]
df_other = df[df['task_id'] != 103]

# 2. Compute Pearson correlations
r1, p1 = stats.pearsonr(df103['QED_delta'], df103['SA_delta'])
r2, p2 = stats.pearsonr(df_other['QED_delta'], df_other['SA_delta'])
n1 = len(df103)
n2 = len(df_other)

# 3. Fisher z-transformation and 95% CI for each
def fisher_ci(r, n, alpha=0.05):
    z = np.arctanh(r)
    se = 1/np.sqrt(n - 3)
    z_crit = stats.norm.ppf(1 - alpha/2)
    lo_z, hi_z = z - z_crit * se, z + z_crit * se
    return np.tanh(lo_z), np.tanh(hi_z)

ci1 = fisher_ci(r1, n1)
ci2 = fisher_ci(r2, n2)

# 4. Test difference between correlations
z1 = np.arctanh(r1)
z2 = np.arctanh(r2)
se_diff = np.sqrt(1/(n1-3) + 1/(n2-3))
z_stat = (z1 - z2) / se_diff
p_diff = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))

# 5. Print results
print("Correlation QED_delta vs SA_delta:")
print(f" Task 103: r = {r1:.4f}, 95% CI = [{ci1[0]:.4f}, {ci1[1]:.4f}], p-value = {p1:.3e}, n = {n1}")
print(f" Other tasks: r = {r2:.4f}, 95% CI = [{ci2[0]:.4f}, {ci2[1]:.4f}], p-value = {p2:.3e}, n = {n2}")
print(f"\nFisher z-test comparing correlations: z = {z_stat:.3f}, p-value = {p_diff:.3e}\n")

# 6. Visualization
sns.set(style='whitegrid')
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), sharex=True, sharey=True)

sns.regplot(x='QED_delta', y='SA_delta', data=df103,
            scatter_kws={'s': 10, 'alpha': 0.3}, line_kws={'color': 'red'}, ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title('Task 103')
axes[0].set_xlabel('QED_delta')

sns.regplot(x='QED_delta', y='SA_delta', data=df_other,
            scatter_kws={'s': 10, 'alpha': 0.3}, line_kws={'color': 'blue'}, ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title('Other Tasks')
axes[1].set_xlabel('QED_delta')

axes[0].set_ylabel('SA_delta')
fig.suptitle('QED_delta vs SA_delta with Regression Lines')

# annotate with correlation values
axes[0].text(0.05, 0.9, f"r = {r1:.2f}", transform=axes[0].transAxes)
axes[1].text(0.05, 0.9, f"r = {r2:.2f}", transform=axes[1].transAxes)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])
plt.show()
